name: Opus-fleet small/mid-cap growth
strategy: Concentrated long book in small/mid-cap cloud, AI-infra, and fintech compounders with secular demand, riding small-cap and software leadership while avoiding weak crypto.

positions.thesis: Promoted to largest line because the single fact that capped it has been removed: I held it at 11% only to control gap risk into the 13 August print, and that print delivered the first $1bn net income quarter in company history with 33% ROE and record unit economics across all three markets. It is now the cheapest thing I own at 15.91x forward against mid-30s growth, has the lowest beta in the book at 0.94, and closed at $15.23 back above its $15.06 200-day after basing near a $13.47 50-day, so I am adding to a valuation-supported breakout rather than chasing momentum. Consensus $18.39 leaves 20% open. Critically it is the only holding whose earnings power is driven by Brazilian and Mexican penetration rather than US long-end rates or AI sentiment, which is precisely the diversification a book de-rating on both of those needs. Stop stays wide at -18% because a 16x multiple gives real downside support and I do not want to be shaken out of a post-gap consolidation.

Held unchanged because nothing this week touched the thesis: FY27 guidance still calls for over 80% revenue growth with optical alone above $600m, revenue tripled on the last full year, and the 1 September print sits outside this window so there is no binary to manage. Friday's -2.29% was mild next to the 4-5% taken out of the pure software names, consistent with AI-infra hardware being valued on delivered revenue rather than terminal multiple. I am deliberately not adding despite that relative strength: at beta 3.23 it is already the dominant risk contributor in the book by a wide margin, and in a tape that just showed it will de-rate high-multiple growth on a single soft data point, concentrating further into the highest-beta line would undo the risk reduction I am making elsewhere. Widest stop in the book at -25% for the same beta reason, since anything tighter is noise.

Added three points because Friday proved the diversification claim rather than merely asserting it: XBI closed green while three of my software lines lost 4-5%, and at beta 0.83 across 157 equal-weighted names it carries neither single-drug risk nor the multiple-compression risk that is currently the live threat to the rest of the book. The driver is M&A and improving regulatory sentiment rather than the AI capex cycle every other position keys off, which is genuine low correlation and not just a different ticker. Up 76.6% over the year, so I keep the tighter -15% stop: much of that gain is embedded in my entry price, and the one thing that would break this line is a hike that actually lands, because biotech carries duration too.

Added two points because it was the only software line in the book that rose on a day the group was sold, which says the market has finished digesting the one-large-AI-customer usage scare that knocked it after the print. The event risk is behind it, the FY26 guide went up to $4.45-4.47bn on 36% revenue growth, and 46 analysts at $283.88 leave 11% open, more headroom than NET offers. Still capped below my top holdings rather than promoted further, because the customer-concentration overhang is a real single-counterparty exposure on a name at a very high earnings multiple and one soft usage disclosure could repeat. Stop held at -20% to respect that gap risk.

Cut three points but kept, because the macro case strengthened while the evidence for the position weakened and those net out to a smaller line rather than a binary. Strengthened: with Hammack pushing for immediate hikes and the Fed debate now about tightening, the roughly one-third of revenue that is net interest compounds, and prediction markets growing revenue tenfold in a quarter is a real new engine. Weakened: it is still -12.02% over 52 weeks while the S&P prints records, it lost 3.83% on Friday, and consumer sentiment collapsing to 51.0 with retail sales down 0.6% is a direct headwind to the retail engagement that drives the transaction franchise. I said last week I would not keep feeding a laggard, and sizing it joint-largest at beta 2.32 while a beta-0.94 name at 16x forward is available is the wrong allocation of the same risk budget. Stop stays wide at -22% precisely because the beta guarantees a tighter one would be jumped through.

Trimmed three points to the smallest line because it is the purest expression of the risk Friday actually repriced. The business is fine, with 36% revenue growth, guidance raised on AI-driven demand, and FedRAMP High plus the Kitesurf agent browser as real product momentum, but at 203x forward with a GAAP loss and 34 analysts averaging $333.55 against $315.78 there is only 5.6% of consensus headroom left to pay me for carrying the highest multiple in the book. It fell 4.55%, the worst drop of any holding, on a day the index lost only 0.20%, which is exactly what a long-duration equity does when hike odds turn live. I keep a position because the AI-consumption thesis was validated rather than merely survived, but I will not hold it at conviction size when essentially the entire remaining return has to come from multiple expansion. Stop held tight at -15% to protect the earnings gap rather than round-trip it.

reassessment_note: Weekly desk 2026-08-15: Two binaries I was carrying resolved in opposite directions and the book should reflect that rather than sit through it. I cut NU to 11% purely as gap control into its 13 August print; that print was the best in the company's history and the stock re-took its 200-day, so the reason for the underweight is gone and the correct response to a resolved-bullish event is to restore size, not keep paying for insurance that has already expired. CRWD goes to zero for the mirror reason: I wrote last week that I was paying a premium for opex-scare protection I no longer need, and it is now the only name I own trading above its own sell-side consensus ($216.95 spot against $197.10 across 53 analysts) while carrying a 26 August print inside my window. Holding a negative-expectancy binary purely because the platform is good is not a thesis. The trims to NET and HOOD follow Friday's evidence rather than a forecast: the session was a duration de-rating and not risk-off, so I take weight from the line with the least analyst headroom on the highest multiple (NET, 5.6% to target at 203x) and from the line that has now lagged 12% over 52 weeks while indices print records at beta 2.32 (HOOD). The proceeds go where the rotation is actually paying — NU at 15.9x and beta 0.94, XBI at beta 0.83 on an M&A wave, DDOG with its event behind it and 11% still open — which drops book beta from roughly 1.52 to 1.43 and makes my largest position the cheapest and lowest-beta one. Cash rises 13% to 16% at 4% APY because retail sales turning negative with sentiment at 51 and a live hike debate is a real reason to hold optionality, not idleness. Turnover is about 25% of NAV at ~2bps a side, immaterial against the risk being repriced.
novelty: I run no Round-2 book, so no same-direction overlap constraint binds here; what distinguishes this book is that it now leads with a low-beta 16x-forward LatAm fintech compounder rather than the high-multiple US software cluster every growth mandate crowds into, and it holds zero cybersecurity and zero crypto.
research_notes: Checked the 14 Aug close on every line plus macro. Tape: SPY -0.20% and the S&P 500 printed a record 7,816.70 Thursday, but Friday split hard by duration — NET -4.55% ($315.78), CRWD -3.80% ($216.95), HOOD -3.83% ($95.56), CRDO -2.29% ($259.90) against DDOG +1.28% ($255.46), XBI +0.35% ($157.41), NU +9.33% ($15.23), and IWM +0.52% to $305.09, a hair off its $305.18 52-week high. That is a multiple de-rating inside a rotation small caps are winning, not broad risk-off. Macro drivers: July PPI flat and CPI moderating, but retail sales -0.6% (first decline in nine months, vs +0.1% expected) and UMich sentiment 55.2 -> 51.0, with the Fed debate now about a HIKE (Cleveland's Hammack calling for immediate increases) that soft inflation merely pushed past September. Names: NU's Q2 on 13 Aug cleared the only binary I was carrying, and cleared it huge — first quarter above $1bn net income, 33% ROE, record unit economics across Brazil/Mexico/Colombia; 15.91x forward, beta 0.94, consensus $18.39 (+20%), and the gap carried it back over its $15.06 200-DMA from a $13.47 50-DMA. CRWD: 53 analysts average $197.10 against $216.95 spot, i.e. 9% BELOW the price, with earnings 26 Aug inside my window and a -3.8% break Friday. NET: 34 analysts at $333.55 leaves only 5.6%, on 203x forward with a GAAP loss — thinnest headroom and richest multiple in the book, exactly what Friday sold. DDOG: raised FY26 to $4.45-4.47bn, 46 analysts at $283.88 (+11%), event behind it, and the only software line green Friday. CRDO: FY27 guided to >80% revenue growth with optical >$600m, next print 1 September so no binary this window, but beta 3.23. XBI: beta 0.83, 157 equal-weighted names, +76.6% over the year on M&A and improving regulatory tone. HOOD: still -12.02% over 52 weeks with beta 2.32 even as indices sit at records; consensus $119.82 (+25%) and prediction markets up tenfold are real, but consumer sentiment at 51 is a direct headwind to retail engagement. Net effect on the book: beta falls from roughly 1.52 to 1.43, the largest position becomes the cheapest and lowest-beta one, and no stop was triggered this week.
